$comment: Every distribution in this repository that declares a version nobody can
install, with the reason that state is acceptable. Measured by
`scripts/declared_publication_sweep.py`, guarded by
`tests/architecture/test_declared_publication.py`.
## Why this file exists at all
`test_module_version_sync.py` proves a module's three version surfaces
AGREE. It cannot prove the agreed version EXISTS. `dotmac-integration`
reads 0.1.0a2 on all three surfaces and the version-identity guard passes,
while the newest tag is dotmac-integration-v0.1.0a1 — internal consistency
and publication are different questions, and only the first one had a
guard. A consumer reading the repository, the changelog or
docs/MODULE_CATALOG.md and pinning ==0.1.0a2 gets a resolver error.
## What a row here does and does not mean
A row means the state is KNOWN and someone has said why. It is not
permission to leave it there, and it is emphatically not a reason to edit
the declared version down to match the index: that would make the
repository agree with the registry by discarding the work the number
describes, and the changelog entry for the unpublished version would then
belong to nothing.
The repair is not always a release, either. `dotmac-imports` was reported
as an anomaly BECAUSE it was release-allowlisted with no tag; the ruling
was that the allowlist row was the wrong half, and it was removed rather
than the module published. Two states this file must keep distinct:
* INTENDED — the distribution is meant to be unpublished right now
(`dotmac-auth-oidc`, `dotmac-imports`). The row records the decision so
the next reader does not undo it by dispatching a release.
* OUTSTANDING — a version is genuinely owed to consumers. The row
records evidence a decision still needs. Two worked examples have now
passed through and been removed on release: `dotmac-integration`
0.1.0a2 (released as a3) and `dotmac-kernel` 0.1.0a67. A row that
expires on its own release is the healthiest shape an entry here has.
Both are recorded the same way and neither is a pass. The reason text is
where the difference lives, which is why the guard requires a premise
rather than a label.
## Two directions, both failures
A distribution entering this state without a row fails — that is a version
silently promised to consumers. A row whose distribution has since been
published ALSO fails and must be removed in the same change as the release,
because a ledger that only grows stops describing anything (ADR-0018).
## The oracle is a git tag
The release workflows write a tag only after `verify-registry` has
installed the exact published version from the private index and registered
its manifest, so a tag is this repository's own assertion that a version is
installable — stronger than 'an upload succeeded'. The index is not queried
directly: that needs an authenticated URL, which makes the check
un-runnable at PR time and offline, and a gate that cannot run is not a
gate. The stated cost is that a publication whose tag step failed reads
here as unpublished — which is exactly the state
`recover-module-release.yml` exists to repair, so reporting it is correct.

dotmac-brand-profiles.reason: INTENDED UNTIL THE ADR-0033 COHORT RELEASE. ADR-0033 s2a built this owner product-first from Sub BrandProfile; EXTRACTION.toml is audit-complete with empty adoption_evidence and no product pins it. Two adopters, two different obligations: Sub is the first and its cutover renders BOTH colour pipelines and diffs the output, because the migrated colours are the same VALUES rendered by a different generator (dotmac-ui supersedes Sub brand_theme.py); the vendor control plane is the second and composes the PLATFORM plane greenfield with no migration and no render diff owed. The semantic_colors reduction is RULED (2026-08-19) and dispositioned in code. The render diff is owed by Sub's cutover, not by the tag. RELEASE IS NOT ADOPTION, and this row no longer pretends otherwise: it was written to say the row goes when the adoption evidence lands, which made the cutover unreachable by construction - dotmac_vendor_control_plane cannot pin an unpublished module, so gating the tag on the adoption it enables is a deadlock, the same one dotmac-ticketing, dotmac-integration and dotmac-application-directory each record having broken. The module is now release-allowlisted, which makes it PUBLISHABLE and asserts nothing more. The row is removed by the release change that tags the ADR-0033 cohort (kernel 0.1.0a77 plus all four modules) just in time for the cutover named below - the dotmac-imports pattern, not ahead of it - and the obligations listed here stay enforced where they are enforceable: in EXTRACTION.toml, whose adoption_evidence stays empty and whose first_cutover stays 'Not started' until the adopting product proves them.

dotmac-kernel.reason: INTENDED UNTIL THE ADR-0033 VENDOR MODULE COHORT RELEASES. This kernel version adds one MIGRATION_OWNER_LEDGER row and no behaviour — the allocation for a module in the same change. A kernel whose only content is an allocation has no consumer until that module exists, so it is published together with the module it allocates for, not ahead of it. The module floors already pin this exact version, so releasing the kernel alone would satisfy nothing. Remove this row in the release change that tags the kernel and its module together; do NOT edit the declared version down, which would discard the allocation the number describes.

dotmac-campaigns.reason: INTENDED UNTIL PRODUCT-FIRST CUTOVER. The audited campaign lifecycle and exact-commit Observer validation are complete; kernel a73 and Durable Timers a1 are registry-verified, but current Sub authority evidence still blocks adoption: Sub pins kernel a50, does not compose its lineage, and records consent, idempotency and outbox as unresolved S7+ owner collisions. ADR-0032 requires those cutovers and Sub as the first campaigns authority, using the released kernel/timer contracts. Publishing earlier would create installable parallel owners beside the qualifying source. Remove this row only in the release change that records Sub as the first contract consumer and verifies the exact kernel, timers and campaigns artifacts; do not edit the declared version down.

dotmac-imports.reason: RULED AND RESOLVED 2026-08-15: intended state, not a defect. The sweep first reported this as an anomaly because the module sat in .github/release-modules.json with no dotmac-imports-v tag in any version. The anomaly was the ALLOWLIST ROW, not the missing tag — the package's own EXTRACTION.toml next_action says to keep it audit-complete and unreleased until a real first adopter is ready, and to publish the exact kernel/imports releases just in time for that cutover. Michael ruled: remove the row, do NOT publish. The row is gone from release-modules.json, release-module.yml and recover-module-release.yml; the package keeps its declared 0.1.0a2, its catalogue entry, its kernel floor and its dossier. It is re-added with ERP's adoption proof (cutover 1, gated behind the E8 Organization-to-Tenant and composed-lineage decision). DO NOT 'fix' this by dispatching a release — unreleased is the decision.

dotmac-template-studio.reason: Not in any release lane — absent from release-modules.json and release-adapters.json alike — so no workflow can publish it and no consumer can pin it. It is the still-unlisted stand-in the allowlist gate's own sensitivity proof uses (`test_an_unallowlisted_package_cannot_be_resolved`), which makes unpublished the consistent state rather than an oversight. It is recorded rather than exempted because 0.2.0a3 is the third declared version of a package that has never had a first release.
